literal_meaning: মুখে ধান শুকানো (drying paddy/rice in the mouth)
figurative_meaning_bn: অনর্গল কথা বলা; চড়বড় করে কথা বলা
figurative_meaning_en: To speak fluently without hesitation; to talk rapidly and incessantly
similar_in_english: To run off at the mouth
example_sentences_in_bangla: সভায় সে মুখে ধান শুকানোর মতো কথা বলতে থাকল।
বাচ্চাটা উত্তেজিত হয়ে মুখে ধান শুকানোর মতো গল্প শোনাতে লাগল।
example_sentences_in_english: In the meeting, he started speaking fluently without pause, like drying rice in his mouth.
The child excitedly began chattering away incessantly.
history: This idiom originates from rural Bengali agrarian life, where drying rice (paddy) is a common activity; it metaphorically describes continuous talking as if the mouth is a drying surface for rice grains, implying effortless and nonstop speech.
note: The idiom reflects the agricultural roots of Bengali culture, evoking imagery of rural life.
